purpose: Top-to-bottom project plan for turning Graft from a small working CLI into a well-documented, contributor-friendly, release-ready utility.

current_state.summary: Graft is a dependency-free Python CLI that scans a directory, writes a JSON manifest, and refreshes Markdown inventory tables between stable markers.

planning_principles: Keep runtime dependencies at zero unless a feature clearly cannot be built with the Python standard library.
Prefer small, reviewable changes over large rewrites.
Keep public-facing README content concise and move deeper process notes into docs/.
Protect human-authored Markdown outside generated inventory markers.
Make contributor tasks concrete, labeled, and testable.
Use check mode and tests as the guardrails for generated content behavior.

project_plan.name: Foundation and repository posture
project_plan.goal: Make the repository safe, understandable, and ready for contributors before feature expansion.

tasks.title: Choose and add a project license
tasks.rationale: The repository currently has no explicit reuse permissions, so contributors and users need a clear license before public distribution or packaging.
acceptance_criteria: Add a LICENSE file at the repository root.
Update README.md so it no longer says license permissions are undecided.
Confirm the chosen license matches the maintainer's intended reuse posture.

tasks.title: Keep support documentation organized under docs/
tasks.rationale: Support docs should not crowd the root README. The root should remain a clean landing page while docs/ holds deeper process material.
acceptance_criteria: Move notes and contributing material into docs/.
Keep root-level support-doc duplicates removed.
Update CLI defaults and inventories so docs/notes.md is the notes target.

tasks.title: Document issue labels and project taxonomy
tasks.rationale: A small repo still needs consistent labels so issues are easy to sort and contributors know what kind of work is available.
acceptance_criteria: Add docs/issue_labels.md.
Document label categories for priority, type, status, and miscellaneous states.
Use the label taxonomy when creating future issues.

project_plan.name: Documentation and onboarding
project_plan.goal: Give users and contributors enough context to run, understand, and improve the project without needing private chat history.

tasks.title: Add example workflows and CLI usage docs
tasks.rationale: Concrete examples make the CLI easier to understand and give new contributors safe documentation work to start with.
acceptance_criteria: Add docs/examples.md or an equivalent examples document.
Document at least three copy-pasteable commands.
Include examples for scanning a repository, scanning a subfolder, custom output targets, and using check mode.

tasks.title: Maintain architecture documentation
tasks.rationale: Architecture notes explain the flow from CLI parsing to scanning, rendering, writing, and check-mode validation.
acceptance_criteria: Add docs/architecture.md.
Describe the core flow and InventoryGenerator responsibilities.
Keep architecture notes updated when core behavior changes.

tasks.title: Maintain project workflow documentation
tasks.rationale: Maintainer workflow docs keep issue handling, PR review, CI checks, and release routines consistent.
acceptance_criteria: Add docs/maintainer_workflow.md.
Document issue handling, pull request review, CI, releases, and documentation upkeep.
Reference docs/CONTRIBUTING.md and docs/issue_labels.md where appropriate.

tasks.title: Refresh README and notes inventories after documentation moves
tasks.rationale: The README inventory should reflect the final docs/ layout and should not list moved root files.
acceptance_criteria: Run or manually apply the generated inventory update after docs are moved.
Ensure README.md lists docs/CONTRIBUTING.md and docs/notes.md, not root copies.
Ensure docs/notes.md inventory is current.

project_plan.name: CLI safety and usability
project_plan.goal: Make Graft safer to preview, easier to verify, and more pleasant to use in real repositories.

tasks.title: Implement optional dry-run mode for CLI
tasks.rationale: A dry-run mode would let users preview manifest and Markdown inventory changes without touching files.
acceptance_criteria: Add a --dry-run CLI option.
Print which files would be created or updated.
Do not modify files while dry-run mode is active.
Add tests that prove files are left unchanged.

tasks.title: Expand tests for check mode
tasks.rationale: Check mode is the core CI guardrail and should be tested for both passing and stale-output cases.
acceptance_criteria: Test check mode returns zero when generated files are current.
Test check mode returns non-zero when README inventory is stale.
Test check mode returns non-zero when manifest is missing or stale.

tasks.title: Add tests for custom README, notes, and manifest targets
tasks.rationale: Custom output paths are part of the CLI contract and should stay stable.
acceptance_criteria: Test --readme writes to a custom Markdown file.
Test --notes writes to a custom Markdown file.
Test --manifest writes JSON to a custom path.

project_plan.name: Generated artifact policy
project_plan.goal: Decide how generated manifests and inventory examples should be represented without creating noisy diffs for normal users.

tasks.title: Decide whether generated manifest.json should be tracked
tasks.rationale: Generated manifests are useful examples, but tracking them by default can create noisy diffs in real projects.
acceptance_criteria: Record the tracking policy in documentation.
Keep manifest.json ignored unless a tracked example is intentionally added.
Update README.md or docs/examples.md with the chosen guidance.

tasks.title: Add a tiny example project fixture
tasks.rationale: A tiny example fixture would show users what Graft changes look like without requiring them to experiment on their own repo.
acceptance_criteria: Add a small examples/ directory only if the manifest tracking policy allows it.
Include a before/after style explanation in docs/examples.md.
Avoid creating a large or noisy sample project.

project_plan.name: Packaging and release readiness
project_plan.goal: Prepare Graft for safe installation, tagging, and possible publication once the license and CLI surface are stable.

tasks.title: Define versioning and release process
tasks.rationale: The package has version metadata, but maintainers need a clear process for bumps, tags, and release notes.
acceptance_criteria: Document when to bump patch, minor, or major versions.
Document release checklist in docs/maintainer_workflow.md.
Keep pyproject.toml version aligned with tags.

tasks.title: Review package name before publication
tasks.rationale: The local package metadata uses graft-inventory. Before publishing, confirm the name, command, and README language are final.
acceptance_criteria: Confirm package name availability and intent.
Confirm console script name remains graft.
Update README install guidance once publication is planned.

tasks.title: Add release-focused CI checks when ready
tasks.rationale: Basic CI exists now. Release CI can wait until package publication is a real goal.
acceptance_criteria: Add package build validation.
Validate metadata with standard Python packaging tools if dependencies are acceptable for development only.
Keep runtime dependency-free even if development tooling is added.

project_plan.name: Future feature polish
project_plan.goal: Add useful features only after the core contract is stable and well-tested.

tasks.title: Consider manifest comparison mode
tasks.rationale: Comparing old and new manifests could help maintainers understand what changed between scans.
acceptance_criteria: Define expected input format for old and new manifests.
Print added, removed, and changed files clearly.
Add tests for comparison output.

tasks.title: Consider machine-readable check output
tasks.rationale: JSON output for check mode could make Graft easier to integrate into dashboards or bots.
acceptance_criteria: Add an opt-in flag such as --json.
Keep normal human-readable output unchanged by default.
Document schema and add tests.

tasks.title: Improve summaries for more file types
tasks.rationale: Better summaries make inventories more useful, but parser expansion should stay conservative and dependency-free.
acceptance_criteria: Identify file types that can be summarized safely with simple text rules.
Avoid heavyweight parsers.
Add tests for each new extractor.

next_best_actions: Refresh README.md and docs/notes.md inventories so they reflect the final docs/ layout.
Create issues for needed tasks that do not yet have issue numbers, starting with check-mode coverage and custom target tests.
Resolve the license decision before public distribution or package publication.
Add docs/examples.md to make the CLI workflow copy-pasteable.
Implement --dry-run once tests around current write behavior are stronger.

issue_creation_queue.title: Refresh generated inventories after docs reorganization
Expand test coverage for check mode
Add tests for custom output targets

maintenance_notes: Keep this file hand-editable and dependency-free.
When an issue closes, update the matching task status.
When a new issue is created from issue_creation_queue, move or link it into the relevant project_plan phase.
Prefer small suggestions that are easy for contributors to understand and verify.
Treat this file as the project map, not as generated output from the CLI.
